newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money settles down after sharp hike.
newsitem.headline: German call money settles down after sharp hike.

text.p: German call money rates eased back on Friday after being racheted up to almost 4.25 percent in the previous session as banks rushed for funds to meet their end-of-the-month obligations.

With a new month beginning on Friday, rates stabilised back down to around 3.07 to 3.08 percent. Traders said they expected the rate to ease further on Monday as the overhang from Thursday's scurry higher wore off.
"We're still in a swap-over phase at the moment," said one Frankfurt-based trader. "But call money rates are recovering."
Data from the Bundesbank showed that banks held 45.4 billion marks at the the central bank on Thursday, up from 42.8 billion marks on Wednesday, giving an everage for the month of 41.3 billion marks.
With month-end scrambling for funds, around 4.3 billion marks was borrowed from the Lambard emergency facility.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.09580 percent on Friday, substantially lower than 4.32500 percent on Thursday.
